physicalDetails.detail: Stout man in a smock gone grey to the elbows with flour; stands in the high granary doorway with his cap pushed back and arms folded.

voiceMarkers.detail: Not heard directly. Seen pointing at the hoist beam and 'away west along the road, talking'. Reported 'pleased with the price'.

beliefs.belief: The new man is a good seller and a nice young fellow; the flour is a bargain.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Wrong; he has been selling the contaminated flour to the village for three months.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Not shown; Brask means to question him 'first thing' and 'hear from Joss what he knows about this lad' (Tam).

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Unknown; his granary and yard burn. He is at home asleep when the loft is found.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Bought his grain from the valley farms for twenty years; three months ago started buying barley and flour from a new young man with a cart (cheaper by two coppers on the measure): four loads, the last a fortnight ago; shared a jug with the man at the alehouse; hired Tam at the back end of summer; showed Cyndia the sacks in the loft; dropped the bar on the outside of the granary at suppertime.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Arms folded, cap back; unfolds them to point.

knowledge.detail: Knows the young man: young, civil, brown or fair hair (uncertain), a good horse; bought him a jug the first time and asked after Joss's wife's leg; 'He'd know him again, he says.' Knows the flour's sack source as the young man's cart, from the west road. Does not know it is poisoned. Does not know what is under his loft floorboard (or does he).

arc.lie: He is dealing with a good new seller.
arc.currentPosition: Unknowing dupe or accomplice (open); owner of the burned granary; Brask will question him in the morning (off-page).
